VISUAL STYLE: match the visual style of the reference game shown in the attached reference sheets as closely as possible. Study them for rendering, palette, brushwork, materials, shape language and UI finish, then render our content as if it were made by the same art team. Do NOT output UV maps, texture atlases or a collage of the sheets; output one coherent finished image. Style traits to reproduce: stylized 3D game look, low-poly chunky bevelled forms whose volume is read through hand-painted textures with visible brush strokes and baked light/shadow plus soft rim light; chibi proportions about 3 to 3.5 heads tall, big readable head silhouettes, thin angular shoulders, distinct oversized props; friendly rounded heroes vs. angular segmented creatures with carapaces, spikes and golden eyes; warm/cool complementary colors (teal/cyan bodies, coral and sand armor plates, gold accents, deep maroon or navy shadows, never pure black), purple 'dark/corrupted' variants; magic as pure neon color with near-white cores and glow (fire orange-yellow, ice cyan-white, lightning electric blue, acid lime, dark purple), thin shapes like rings, diamonds and trails; each world has a saturated signature fog color, floors and props desaturated so characters and spells pop; top-down 3/4 perspective camera; UI made of dark organic stone: purple-grey bevelled stone buttons, black spiky organic frames around bars, lava-orange health fill, yellow highlights. CONTENT comes from our own game script below; all characters, creatures and places are ours: do not reproduce any specific existing character, creature, logo or game title from the reference one-to-one. No readable text, letters, numbers, watermark or logos; use abstract glyph-like marks where text would go.

CONTENT: Environment sheet in the same layout as the canonical crypt kit: left, a finished top-down 3/4 playable area with the named hero for scale and a few enemies; right, the modular kit laid out (floor tiles, walls, props, destructibles, light sources, interactables).
